fixes.title: Fix: Unnecessary sales escalation
fixes.summary: 3 failing runs graded by jev-demo-decision-failure. Evidence: “review: Prospect said the new plan was all they needed and bought online; the AE cycle added a week and no value.”. Method failure: the fix is a procedure, jev-demos/lead_routing/lh400-s11/senselab/procedure-unnecessary-sales-escalation, for the next run to follow.

corrective_entry.value: {"goal": "Avoid unnecessary AE escalation by aligning the decision with the prospect\u2019s stated procurement intent and channel.", "steps": ["Extract intent and procurement-channel signals from the message: (a) explicit request for a demo/walkthrough or sales conversation; (b) statement that a new plan is sufficient or they already bought online; (c) trial already started and they want to roll out without requesting a demo; (d) mention of purchasing via a local vendor or needing in\u2011country invoicing; (e) pricing/quote request without a meeting request.", "If (a) is true, decide: route_to_ae.", "If (b) or (c) is true, decide: self_serve.", "If (d) is true, do not escalate; decide: self_serve and note the reseller/in\u2011country invoicing constraint in the review.", "If only (e) is true, decide: self_serve.", "If none apply, follow segment guidance; when ambiguous, prefer self_serve initially rather than routing to AE."], "on_failure": "If signals conflict or are unclear, choose self_serve and note what was ambiguous; do not route_to_ae unless the demo/walkthrough request is explicit.", "verify": "Before choosing route_to_ae, confirm there is an explicit demo/walkthrough request and no evidence like \u201cbought online/new plan sufficient\u201d or \u201clocal vendor/in\u2011country invoicing.\u201d"}

manifest.rationale: The judge flagged unnecessary escalation: “review: Prospect said the new plan was all they needed and bought online; the AE cycle added a week and no value.” and “review: Prospect told the AE they purchase through a local vendor with in-country invoicing; closed-lost.” In failing runs the agent still chose {"action": "route_to_ae"}. The passing runs show conditions to preserve: AE is correct when there’s an explicit walkthrough request — “Looking to see the product in action — can someone walk us through it this week? … decision: route_to_ae … review: Closed-won in 32 days.” and self_serve is correct when only pricing/activation is needed — “decision: self_serve … review: Signed up and activated within a week.” The procedure adds an explicit verification step for procurement intent and channel before escalating, directs self_serve when the prospect already bought online/only needs plan activation or mentions a local vendor/in-country invoicing, and preserves AE routing only when a demo/walkthrough is explicitly requested.

corrective_entry.value:
Risk: Unclear escalation path in post-decision reviews can create misleading negative lessons for mid_market/emea partner routing.
Evidence seen in failing runs:
- "review: Escalated later by a different team; root cause unclear."
- {"kind": "lesson", "text": "Went badly for reasons outside the decision; flagged by the reviewing team.", "action": "decide:partner", "worked": false, "situation": "mid_market/emea"} (read as learned-mid-market-emea-5b6fddc3 v31/v35, evidence_status: discredited)
Guidance: When a review cites an escalation by a different team or says the root cause is unclear, do not treat it as a failure of the decision (e.g., decide:partner) and do not record or rely on a 'worked: false' lesson. Instead, mark the review as 'inconclusive/ops escalation', seek owner/clarification, and continue to rely on validated lessons for this segment. Ignore any learned-* entries with these ambiguous review phrases until verified.

manifest.rationale: Two failing runs read discredited versions of learned-mid-market-emea-5b6fddc3 that said “Went badly for reasons outside the decision; flagged by the reviewing team.” and “Escalated later by a different team; root cause unclear.” The judge failures quote these exact phrases. In 88c2019e… the agent read v35 (discredited) and in 83e4881… it read v31 (discredited). The third failing run (4e038e7…) showed the same ambiguous review without a memory read, indicating a workflow issue with how such reviews are interpreted. The current live entry (v36) reads “Partner closed the deal in 24 days.” (worked: true), so no correction to that fact is needed. Adding a risk belief instructs the agent not to treat unclear escalations as decision failures, to ignore/withhold such negative lessons until verified, and to rely on validated lessons instead, which should prevent the unclear-escalation-path failure from recurring while leaving passing runs unaffected.

fixes.title: Fix: Unexplained rejection
fixes.summary: 3 failing runs graded by jev-demo-decision-failure. Evidence: “review: Reviewer marked this one a miss; no detail recorded.”.

corrective_entry.value: When reviewer feedback is only "Reviewer marked this one a miss; no detail recorded.", do not treat it as a lesson or use any lesson whose text equals that to drive a decide:<action>. Ignore such lessons if retrieved and base routing on explicit policy signals (company size, region, role, stated intent, and business email). If signals are mixed, lower confidence or choose the safer SDR nurture path and include rationale. Evidence: failing traces show the exact note in review, and one run read a lesson whose text was exactly that and was marked discredited.

manifest.rationale: All three failing runs include the reviewer note: "Reviewer marked this one a miss; no detail recorded." The tool calls succeeded (e.g., {"action": "partner", "confidence": 0.96}) but were rejected post-hoc without guidance. In trace 23ad5b63-9c7d-410c-8bfc-650551217c4d a discredited memory was read: value {"kind": "lesson", "text": "Reviewer marked this one a miss; no detail recorded.", "action": "decide:partner", "worked": false, "situation": "mid_market/emea"}. This shows an uninformative reviewer note had been turned into a decision-driving lesson. Adding a belief to ignore such notes as lessons and rely on explicit routing signals should prevent repeats of this unexplained rejection pattern without disturbing other behaviors.

items.name: Unnecessary sales escalation
items.description: The agent routes or extends the human sales process after the buyer already committed or purchased through another channel, adding time and no value. This pattern occurs when the agent fails to confirm purchase intent or channel before escalating to an AE.

items.name: Unclear escalation path
items.description: A decision or action is later escalated by another team without a documented root cause or clear ownership, leaving reviewers unable to determine why the failure occurred. This pattern hides responsibility and prevents corrective actions because the chain of events and rationale are not recorded.

items.name: Unexplained rejection
items.description: Agent marks items as failures or rejects outputs without providing any rationale or supporting details, leaving reviewers unable to diagnose or reproduce the issue.

items.name: Recovered after error
items.description: A tool or step failed during the run and the agent recovered: it retried successfully, used a fallback, or told the user what went wrong.

items.name: Properly handled
items.description: The agent completed the task correctly: no judge found an unsupported claim, a missing tool call, a retry loop or an unhandled error.
